label: hold
definition: One shot longer than the generation window, continued across units. Not an edit. The seam exists only because the runtime has a maximum clip length, and it must read as no seam at all. The strictest pin set in the grammar, because nothing is supposed to be happening here.
refuses_when: The delta carries anything but a temporal advance. A HOLD that changes framing is a CARRY that was mislabelled.

label: carry
definition: Camera keeps moving and the subject continues. The highest continuity demand that is still an editorial choice rather than a runtime artifact.
refuses_when: The outgoing unit's hands-forward motion is absent from the incoming unit's accepts set. An orbit welded to a locked-off static is a visible stop, and the grammar refuses it before the GPU finds out.

label: reframe
prior_era_counterpart: a cut within a scene, on the same setup
definition: Same scene, new framing. Composition shifts and scene facts hold. Still predicted, because the reference remains useful across it.
refuses_when: Lens and subject scale are deliberately unpinned — a reframe that could not change them would be a carry. Refuses when the prompt diff touches environment or grade, which are SPS scope.

label: cut
prior_era_counterpart: the forced IDR; the cement splice
definition: A deliberate new shot. The reference is useless across it, so the unit stands on nothing earlier: fresh latent seed, full prompt, no anchor. This is the condition the codec calls a scene cut, and it is the only seam that is free by construction.
refuses_when: A P-Node is emitted instead. A cut welded to its predecessor is the specific failure the intra decision exists to prevent, and it presents as a morph.

label: marked seam
definition: An I-Node the director asks for so the shot stays independently re-cuttable, whether or not the content demands one. Costs bytes, buys editability — the format's single strongest lever, spent deliberately.
refuses_when: Nothing. This class exists precisely so that wanting a seam is a sufficient reason to have one, and the cost is stated rather than hidden.

label: match cut
definition: An I-Node across which one named quantity is asserted to agree — a shape mask, a motion-vector angle, a dominant hue — measured on the last frame before and the first frame after, within a declared tolerance.
refuses_when: The named invariant is absent from either side, or the measured difference exceeds tolerance. A match cut whose match is not checkable is a cut with a note attached.

label: graft
definition: A seam whose two sides were produced by different engines or different model weights. Forces an I-Node because a P-Node's delta is meaningless against an anchor another model made. The SPS/EPS boundary moves with it.
refuses_when: The two sides' evidence records name the same engine and the same weights digest — that is a CUT, and calling it a graft overstates the discontinuity.

label: dissolve
prior_era_counterpart: the optical printer dissolve; the NLE cross-fade
definition: Not a SYN construct at all. Both sides exist as independent instruction chains and the blend is a transition parameter on an A-track cut pointer, applied to finished frames.
refuses_when: It is declared in SYN. A blend a generative model produced across two prompts is a morph, and calling it a dissolve is the mislabel this class exists to prevent.
